summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing network peering, routing issues, and recent runtime upgrade. Discussed perf regressions with long-sequence KV cache misses, NAT gateway throughput limits, and next steps to run focused benchmarks and exchange security docs.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Gonzalez (CTO - Catalyst), Sana Patel (Platform), Jordan Li (Security), Evelyn Ruiz (DevOps)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everybody, thanks for joining — we'll kick off. Quick agenda: peering status, the runtime 1.4.2 upgrade fallout, KV cache hit-rate observations, and next steps. Sana, you good to start with peering update?
[00:18] Sana (Catalyst): Yeah, thanks Alex. We finished the VPC peering config yesterday but saw a weird routing flap when we hit the NAT gateway. So, the peering itself is established, routes propagated, but egress to Redwood's control plane IPs timed out on a few bursts.
[00:45] Evelyn (Catalyst): Just to add, our infra team increased the NAT gateway concurrent connections and we saw improvement, but there were still occasional 504-like timeouts. Could be throttling on the egress or SG rules.
[01:10] Priya (Redwood): Ok thanks. We're seeing similar behavior when the runtime tries to fetch model shards during cold starts — if the KV cache isn't warmed the additional upstream requests hit the egress path. That amplifies the NAT gateway pressure.
[01:42] Mark (Catalyst): Right — on the first run after a restart we saw 600-700ms p95, then spikes to 2-3s on some sequences. Is that KV miss related?
[02:05] Priya (Redwood): Likely. Our instrumentation showed KV cache hit-rate drop from usual ~94% to ~68% under the workload pattern you ran (lots of long sequences, stepwise). We also merged the 1.4.2 runtime which changed how we shard KV and that could've affected cold path.
[02:32] Jordan (Catalyst): Quick Q on KMS — we need to confirm HSM vs KMS key policy before you rotate keys. Also, was there any change in telemetry or audit log endpoints with 1.4.2?
[02:53] Alex (Redwood): Good Q. No change to the audit endpoints; we updated internal kernel selection but audit footprint is the same. For KMS we have both options; we can support customer-managed keys in KMS and HSM workflows — Jordan, can you send the exact policy requirements and we'll map them?
[03:20] Jordan (Catalyst): Yep will send today.
[03:34] Priya (Redwood): Back to the NAT issue — two immediate mitigations: 1) increase NAT throughput / add a second NAT gateway per AZ, 2) enable prefix-level egress routing to reduce SNAT pressure, or 3) use a VPC endpoint to our control plane if your staging allows it. Which is easiest for you?
[04:05] Evelyn (Catalyst): For production we'd prefer VPC endpoints, but for the POC we can spin up an additional NAT gateway to validate.
[04:22] Mark (Catalyst): Can Redwood provide a short checklist for optimum routing config? We had a couple of security folks uncomfortable with broad open egress rules.
[04:40] Alex (Redwood): Absolutely — I'll send the recommended routing/security checklist. We'll include minimal necessary outbound CIDRs, port ranges, and a sample iptables/SG template (note: we sometimes see ports mis-typed as Samal in earlier docs, but we'll be explicit).
[05:05] Priya (Redwood): Also, we want to run a focused KV-cache benchmark that simulates your long-seq workload. Plan is 1k requests, varying seq length 128/512/1024 tokens, measure p50/p95/p99 and hit-rate. We'll share the script and results.
[05:33] Sana (Catalyst): Great, that would help. Also curious if there were any config flags changed in 1.4.2 that could explain the hit-rate delta.
[05:48] Priya (Redwood): There was a small change in the cache eviction heuristic — it now favors smaller prefetched prefixes to reduce memory pressure, which can lower hit-rate for some patterns. We can toggle that back in a branch for your tests and compare.
[06:12] Mark (Catalyst): If toggling that helps, what is the CPU/memory tradeoff? We have limited GPU RAM for the pilot.
[06:30] Priya (Redwood): Good point. Reverting the heuristic increases memory by ~8-12% on our internal runs and reduces cold-start overhead by improving hit-rate. We'll include those numbers in the benchmark report.
[07:00] Alex (Redwood): On the upgrade timeline — you mentioned you applied 1.4.2 earlier this week, correct?
[07:12] Evelyn (Catalyst): Yes, we rolled it to the staging cluster Tuesday night. Production is still on 1.3.x.
[07:25] Alex (Redwood): For safety we recommend keeping prod on 1.3.x until we confirm the KV behaviour under your workload. We'll support a canary of 1.4.2 with controlled traffic.
[07:44] Jordan (Catalyst): For security review — will that require additional approvals if we run a canary in prod?
[07:55] Alex (Redwood): Usually we treat canary as maintenance; but if you want, we can provide a short risk assessment and rollback checklist for your security team. I'll include that in the pack.
[08:14] Mark (Catalyst): That helps. Also want to understand rollback time — under your observed worst-case, how long to revert a rollout?
[08:30] Priya (Redwood): Typically 2-5 minutes to shift traffic, but stateful KV warming will resume over minutes depending on workload; we'll include expected timelines.
[08:55] Sana (Catalyst): On peering, we also need to confirm whether routes are static or dynamic — our team saw route propagation delays when using dynamic. Could static routes be better here?
[09:12] Alex (Redwood): Static route for the peering egress to the control plane can reduce propagation delays. We'll add recommended route table entries in the checklist.
[09:36] Priya (Redwood): A quick note on metrics: please turn on token-level tracing for the 1k-run benchmark so we can see where misses happen. Token-level traces are noisy but useful for root cause.
[09:55] Evelyn (Catalyst): OK we can enable that for staging.
[10:08] Alex (Redwood): Switching topics — the logs indicated a couple of TLS handshake errors around 02:14 UTC yesterday. We suspect intermittent MTU mismatch on the peered path — can you confirm MTU settings across the path?
[10:28] Evelyn (Catalyst): We'll check, I know our peering partner had jumbo frames disabled by default.
[10:40] Jordan (Catalyst): Also, for KMS rotations, we'll need a maintenance window; if the rotation is required during the POC we have to coordinate dates.
[10:55] Alex (Redwood): Understood — we'll discuss rotation windows after Jordan shares policy.
[11:06] Priya (Redwood): Regarding observability, Alex will send a sample dashboard for per-route latency and token cost so you can track unit economics during the pilot.
[11:23] Alex (Redwood): Yep, will include per-route dashboards and a short guide on interpreting p50/p95 token cost breakdowns.
[11:40] Mark (Catalyst): On the commercial side — are there any changes to the POC quotas if we move to an on-prem pilot?
[11:55] Alex (Redwood): For Private on-prem, quotas shift to a reserved-capacity model. For the POC we'll keep it flexible; if you commit to a dedicated pool we'll provide a pricing sketch. I'll follow up with finance.
[12:12] Priya (Redwood): Back to troubleshooting — immediate plan: Catalyst spins up an extra NAT gateway in staging, Redwood runs the 1k KV benchmark with both default and reverted heuristic, and we'll compare.
[12:28] Sana (Catalyst): Timeline: we can have the NAT change by EOD tomorrow and share peering CIDRs today.
[12:40] Alex (Redwood): Great. I'll send the security pack + routing checklist by Friday (2026-03-20). Priya to post benchmark results by Monday (2026-03-23).
[12:58] Jordan (Catalyst): Quick check: any known incompatibilities with our on-prem hyperconverged nodes? We've got a small HCI cluster for eventual on-prem run.
[13:12] Priya (Redwood): We support our on-prem package on most HCI setups but do require KVM virtualization and a supported kernel (we'll send the compatibility matrix). We'll flag anything extra for your infra.
[13:36] Mark (Catalyst): Can Redwood provide a list of expected metrics and any agent-level ports to open for on-prem?
[13:48] Alex (Redwood): Yes — that's part of the routing checklist. We'll include port list, agents, and sample systemd units.
[14:05] Priya (Redwood): One more note: when we ran your dataset last week in our internal harness we saw a small regression in token throughput after 1.4.2 when using quantized kernels. We'll include those numbers and suggested quantization profile tweaks.
[14:30] Sana (Catalyst): Good to know — quantization is important for cost.
[14:40] Alex (Redwood): Ok we're nearing time. Recap of action items and owners next.
[14:50] Alex (Redwood): Alex — will send security pack + routing checklist + dashboard links by 2026-03-20.
[15:02] Priya (Redwood): Priya — will run KV-cache benchmark (1k requests, 128/512/1024 tokens) and post results with toggled heuristic by 2026-03-23.
[15:16] Evelyn (Catalyst): Evelyn — will share VPC peering info, subnet CIDRs, and confirm MTU by 2026-03-20 and spin up extra NAT by EOD tomorrow.
[15:34] Jordan (Catalyst): Jordan — will send KMS/HSM policy and maintenance window preferences by 2026-03-25.
[15:45] Mark (Catalyst): Mark — follow up on canary approvals, will loop in security once we have the pack.
[15:58] Alex (Redwood): Any final questions?
[16:05] Sana (Catalyst): Nothing else, thanks.
[16:10] Alex (Redwood): Thanks everyone — we'll regroup next Tuesday same time. I'll put notes + links in the calendar invite.

References/Links mentioned: security pack (link to be sent), routing checklist (to be attached), KV benchmark script (repo link to be shared), sample dashboards (link)

End of transcript.
